Thanks for the recap. Confirming BrightBridge's position: we require that data we send to Redwood for inference NOT be used for model training, improvement, or benchmarking by Redwood or its partners. This applies to any internal model tuning or inclusion into model corpora.

Specifics from legal/security:
- PII must be stripped or tokenized prior to transmission where feasible. For the remaining fields we consider PHI; storage is allowed only for 90 days maximum for troubleshooting and audit purposes.
- Audit logs of API calls are acceptable but must be encrypted at rest and only accessible to authorized personnel; retention 90 days.
- Data residency: production processing must happen in us-east-1. If any processing occurs outside that region (e.g., fallback), we require prior notification and written approval.
- We will need an explicit attestation that Redwood will not use our data to train or improve any model without a separate, signed agreement.

Please send the MAP/DPA with the opt-out clause and a short technical appendix describing: cache eviction behavior (KV cache persistence), what appears in logs (URI, timestamps, token counts), and how keys are managed.

Emily —

Thanks for the clear summary and the asks. Below is our formal technical attestation and a short control appendix. I’m attaching a MAP and DPA with the proposed clause for signature.

Technical attestation (summary):
- Training opt-out: Redwood confirms that Customer Data, as defined in the DPA, will NOT be used to train, fine-tune, or benchmark Redwood models without an explicit, signed written agreement. This includes any internal research or partnered model improvement programs.
- Logging & retention: API request metadata (timestamps, model variant, token counts, request/response sizes) and operational logs will be retained for 90 days by default for debugging and audit. Request/response payloads are NOT persisted beyond what is necessary for transient processing unless the customer opts into longer retention or troubleshooting is requested; we will provide a redacted transcript on request.
- KV/cache behavior: Inference KV cache is ephemeral per-session; persistent caches are not written to long-term storage. For cached decoding performance we maintain an in-memory cache that is evicted when the session closes or after 1 hour of inactivity. There is no cross-customer sharing of KV entries.
- Encryption & keys: All stored artifacts (logs, retained troubleshooting data) are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys for Private deployments or REDWOOD-KMS for hosted customers. Access is role-based and logged.
- Data residency: Production inference for BrightBridge will be pinned to the us-east-1 region. Any planned fallback or cross-region processing will be communicated 10 business days ahead and requires written approval.

Attachments:
- redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (control matrix and short appendix)
- mutual-action-plan-BB-001.docx (MAP with proposed clause and sign-off lines)
- dpa-signature-request.pdf (DPA with definitions & data use language)

Emily — please review the attached MAP/DPA. If it matches BrightBridge's requirements we can incorporate the clause verbatim and request a countersignature. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk legal/security through the appendix.
